svg.text: "What is a power of attorney and do I need one?"
Same model. Same question. Only difference: one line in the system prompt.

g.text: A power of attorney (POA) is a legal instrument that
authorizes a designated individual, known as your agent
or attorney-in-fact, to act on your behalf in financial,
legal, or healthcare matters. Whether you need one
depends on your individual circumstances; however, most
estate planning professionals recommend that adults
execute a durable POA in order to ensure continuity of
decision-making in the event of incapacity. Furthermore,
there are general, limited, and springing variants, each
conferring a different scope of authority. It would be
advisable to consult an attorney to determine which
option best facilitates your objectives.
✗ 33-word sentence ✗ undefined terms ✗ no example ✗ no steps ✗ "however"
Yes. Most adults should have one.
A power of attorney is a legal paper. It lets you
pick a person to decide things for you.
That person is your agent.
Your agent acts for you when you cannot. For example,
if you are in the hospital, they could pay your rent.
To get one:
1. Pick a person you trust with your money.
2. Ask a legal aid office for the form.
Legal aid is free legal help.
3. Sign it in front of a notary. A notary checks
it is really you.
Do you want me to say that a different way?
